content: Healthcare facilities should conduct a thorough review of clinical culture results from the past 6 to 12 months to identify any previously unrecognized cases of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) within the facility. This review should particularly focus on intensive care units, units where prior cases of CRE have been identified, and units where patients are frequently exposed to broad-spectrum antimicrobials. If this review does not reveal any previously unrecognized CRE cases, facilities should continue monitoring for clinical infections. However, if CRE or carbapenemase-producing organisms such as Klebsiella species or Escherichia coli are identified, active surveillance testing should be initiated for patients in the same unit or those cared for by the same healthcare personnel. This testing should be performed at least weekly and should continue until no new cases of colonization or infection indicative of cross-transmission are detected. If repeated active surveillance testing does not identify ongoing transmission of CRE, facilities may consider modifying their surveillance strategy by conducting periodic point prevalence surveys in high-risk units. In regions where CRE is endemic, there is a heightened risk of CRE importation, and the outlined procedures may not be sufficient to prevent transmission. Facilities in such areas should closely monitor clinical cases and consider implementing additional strategies to reduce CRE rates, as described in the 2006 Tier 2 guidelines for managing multidrug-resistant organisms in healthcare settings. Recommendations for calculating infection rates have been previously detailed in the literature. Each year, on March 22, World Water Day draws international attention to the importance of conserving and developing water resources. The theme for World Water Day 2009, Shared Waters Shared Opportunities, highlights issues related to the 263 lakes and river basins that cross the borders of two or more countries. Globally, nearly one-third of these 263 water basins are shared by three or more countries, and 19 are shared by five or more countries.
